title: Evaluation of masticatory performance in patients after partial maxillary or mandibular resection and prosthetic-surgical rehabilitation
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate the chewing function of patients after partial resection (partial removal) of the maxilla or mandible and surgical-prosthetic therapy. Chewing is a learned, automatic and complex process in which hard (teeth / dental implants) and soft tissue (tongue, cheek, floor of the mouth) work closely together to grind, move and swallow food safely. The treatment approach for bacterial bone infections (osteomyelitis), keratocysts and head and neck tumors often requires extensive removal (resection) of one or more anatomical structures including the mandible, tongue, floor of the mouth, hard and/or soft palate. In addition to changes in the external appearance, these resections lead in particular to impairments in chewing, swallowing and speaking and often have a detrimental effect on quality of life. These impairments can be exacerbated by radiotherapy. The aim of the study is therefore to examine the chewing performance with regard to the size of the resection, the type of reconstruction and the dental findings and to compare it with the values of patients without resection.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx

interventions.name: patients after partial maxillary or mandibular resection and prosthetic-surgical rehabilitation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients after partial resection of the lower and/or upper jaw and surgical-prosthetic rehabilitation completed > 6 months ago
Exclusion criteria:
- Surgically and prosthetically non-rehabilitated patients
- Fixation of the paraocclusal tray (axiography) in the lower jaw not possible
- Lack of consent from the patient, 
- Patients with dementia or other cognitive impairments who are unable to consent to the study, patients who do not consent to participate in the study for other reasons.
